Rashi on Niddah 39b:10:1.hebrew: א"ל לא אלא הכי א"ר יוחנן כגון דחזיא - תרי זימני בריש ירחא, ופעם שלישית בכ"ה, ורביעית בר"ח; דה"ל הך ראייתה בתרייתא, שהיא שלישית לראייה של ר"ח, בתוך ימי נדותה ממש, שהיא נדה מיום כ"ה; ומש"ה קרי להו תוך ימי נדותה, דהא נדה היא. וטעמא מאי הוי קביעות, הא אורחה בהכי שנפתח מעיינה? משום דאמר: הך ראייה דראש חדש ראיית וסתה היא, והיום זמנה; והאי דאקדים וחזאי בכ"ה — דמים יתירי איתוספו בה:
Rashi on Niddah 39b:10:1.english: He said to him: No, rather, this is what Rabbi Yoḥanan said: For example, where she saw - [She saw blood] twice on Rosh Chodesh, a third time on the twenty-fifth [of the month], and a fourth time on Rosh Chodesh, such that this latest sighting of hers—which is the third sighting on Rosh Chodesh—is literally during the days of her menstruation, as she is a niddah from the twenty-fifth day; and that is why [Rabbi Yoḥanan] calls this "within the days of her menstruation," for she is indeed a niddah. And what is the reason that this constitutes an establishment [of a regular cycle]—is it not her usual way in this manner, once her source has opened? Because he says: This sighting on Rosh Chodesh is the sighting of her regular cycle, and today is its set time; and as for this fact that she saw early on the twenty-fifth, extra blood had accumulated within her.

Rashi on Niddah 39b:11:1.english: They stated it - [Referring to] this [statement] of Rabbi Yoḥanan.

Rashi on Niddah 39b:11:2.english: In accordance with Rav Huna - And as we resolved [it].

Rashi on Niddah 39b:1:1.hebrew: ואמר רב יהודה - דהאי ט"ו היינו לטבילה, שהוא כ"ב לראייתה, ושינתה לכ"ז, וקתני דכי מטי יום כ"ב אסורה לשמש. וקס"ד דהאי כ"ב לאו לראיית הדילוג קאמר, אלא כ"ב לאותו יום שהיתה ראויה לראות בו ודילגתו, דהוי יום י"ז לראייתה, ובתוך ימי זיבה היא לראיית כ"ז:
Rashi on Niddah 39b:1:1.english: And Rav Yehuda said - That this [mention of] fifteen [in the mishna] means [fifteen days] from immersion, which is twenty-two [days] from her sighting, and she changed [her cycle] to [day] twenty-seven; and [the mishna] teaches that when the twenty-second day arrives, she is forbidden to engage in marital relations. And [the Gemara] initially assumed that this [recurrence of] twenty-two is not referring to [twenty-two days from] the sighting of the skip, but rather twenty-two [days] from that day on which she was expected to see and skipped it, which is the seventeenth day from her [actual] sighting, and [thus] she is within the days of ziva relative to the sighting of the twenty-seventh.

Rashi on Niddah 39b:2:1.hebrew: וקתני אסורה - דכי הדר אתו כ"ב לחשבון יום שהיתה ראויה לראות בו כשדילגה, בה קיימא לה בימי זיבה לחשבון ראייתה, כדפרישית. וקסבר רב פפא: יום עשרין ותרתין דאסרינן עלה – מיום כ"ב מנינן, כלומר, לאו כ"ב לראיית דילוגה שהיה בכ"ז, אלא כ"ב מיום שהיתה ראויה לראות לימודה. ומדקרי להו רב פפא ימי זיבה, קסבר: נדה ופתחה – ימי נדותה וזובה – מעשרין וז' מנינן, דהיינו מיום ראיית דילוגה; ומיום ראיית כ"ז עד השתא לא הוו לה י"ז, דאי ליום שראויה לראות כשדילגה מנינן ימי נדות וזוב, לא הוה קרי להו ימי זובה, דהא חלפו להו כ"ב מההוא יומא:
Rashi on Niddah 39b:2:1.english: And it teaches: She is forbidden - For when twenty-two [days] return [and elapse] according to the reckoning of the day on which she was due to see when she skipped, at that time she stands in [her] days of zivah according to the reckoning of her [actual] sighting, as I explained. And Rav Pappa holds: The twenty-second day that we forbid to her, we count from day twenty-two; that is to say, not twenty-two [days] from the sighting of her skip, which was on the twenty-seventh, but rather twenty-two [days] from the day she was due to see according to her established pattern. And from the fact that Rav Pappa calls them "days of zivah," he holds [that the phrase] "niddah and its opening" — the days of her niddah and her zov — we count from the twenty-seventh, which is from the day of the sighting of her skip; and from the day of the sighting on the twenty-seventh until now there were not [more than] seventeen [days]. For if we were to count the days of niddah and zov from the day on which she was due to see when she skipped, he would not have called them the days of her zivah, since twenty-two [days] have already passed from that day.

Rashi on Niddah 39b:3:1.english: Her opening - [The text] refers to the calculation of the days of niddah and zivah as "her opening".

Rashi on Niddah 39b:4:1.hebrew: ממאי - דהאי יום כ"ב דאסרינן ליה, מנינן מיום כ"ב שהיתה ראויה לראות כשדילגה, דמטי ליה בימי זיבה לחשבון ראייה שראתה בכ"ז:
Rashi on Niddah 39b:4:1.english: From where - [Do you know] that this twenty-second day that we prohibit, we count from the twenty-second day on which she was expected to see [blood] when she skipped, so that it falls during the days of zivah according to the calculation of the sighting that she saw on the twenty-seventh?

Rashi on Niddah 39b:4:2.hebrew: דלמא - האי יום כ"ב דאסרינן עלה, מנינן מיום ראייתה, שכבר שלמו ימי זוב כי הדרי אתו הנך כ"ב, וקיימא לה ד' ימים בימים הראוים לנדות:
Rashi on Niddah 39b:4:2.english: Perhaps - This twenty-second day that we forbid to her, we count from the day of her sighting, for the days of zivah have already concluded when those twenty-two [days] arrive, and she stands four days into the days suitable for niddah.

Rashi on Niddah 39b:5:1.hebrew: והכי מסתברא - דהא משום דחיישינן שמא תחזור לקדמותה לראות מכ"ב לכ"ב אסרינן לה, דהשתא הוי כ"ב לראייה. אבל ליום כ"ב לחשבון יום שהיתה ראויה לראות, לא מצי אסרינן משום הא חששא; דאפי' חוזרת לקדמותה, לא תראה היום, שהוא י"ז לראייתה, דההיא לא היתה למודה לראות אלא לכ"ב לראייה. ואי משום שהוא כ"ב ליום הראוי לה — אין זה דרך החוזרת לוסתה לקצר ימי טהרתה ולמהר ימי ראייתה כדי שיבא לפי חשבון של תחלה, אלא חוזרת וקובעת כ"כ ליום שראתה:
Rashi on Niddah 39b:5:1.english: And so it is reasonable - For it is because we are concerned lest she return to her former [routine] of seeing [blood] every twenty-two [days] that we forbid her [to her husband], as now it is twenty-two [days] from [her previous] sighting. But on the twenty-second day according to the reckoning of the day that she was expected to see, we cannot forbid her on account of this concern, for even if she returns to her former [routine], she will not see [blood] today, which is [only] the seventeenth [day] from her sighting, as she was not accustomed to seeing except at twenty-two [days] from [one] sighting [to the next]. And if [one should argue that she might see] because it is twenty-two [days] from the day that was expected for her — it is not the way of [a woman] returning to her regular cycle to shorten her days of purity and hasten her days of sighting so that it should align with the initial reckoning; rather, she returns and establishes [her cycle] likewise from the day that she saw.

Rashi on Niddah 39b:5:2.hebrew: דאלת"ה האי תרנגולתא דרמיא יומא וכבשה יומא ורמיא יומא וכבשה יומא וכבשה תרי יומי ורמיא יומא כי הדרה נקטה כדלקמן נקטה כו' - כלומר, תרנגולת הרגילה להטיל ביצה היום ולעמוד למחר, ולהטיל יום ג' ולעמוד יום ד', ושינתה וסתה, ועמדה מלדת יום ה' עם יום ד', דהוו להו תרי יומי, ורמיא יום ששי. כי הדרה נקטה - אם היא חוזרת למנהגה להטיל יום ולעמוד יום:
Rashi on Niddah 39b:5:2.english: For if you do not say so, this chicken that lays [an egg] one day and withholds [one] day, and lays [one] day and withholds [one] day, and withheld two days and laid [one] day, when it resumes taking hold, does it take hold according to what is ahead, etc. - That is: A chicken that is accustomed to lay an egg today and pause tomorrow, and to lay on the third day and pause on the fourth day; and it changed its regular pattern and paused from laying on the fifth day along with the fourth day, which makes two days, and laid on the sixth day. "When it resumes taking hold" – If it returns to its routine of laying one day and pausing one day.

Rashi on Niddah 39b:6:1.hebrew: כדלקמיה נקטה - מעכשיו היא חוזרת למנות, כגון שעומדת יום ז' שאחר יום ו' שהטילה, ומטלת יום שמיני:
Rashi on Niddah 39b:6:1.english: It adopts according to what is ahead of it - From now on it resumes counting; for example, where it pauses on the seventh day, which is after the sixth day on which it laid [an egg], and lays on the eighth day.

Rashi on Niddah 39b:6:2.hebrew: או כדמעיקרא נקטה - לפי חשבון שהיתה ראויה להטיל מתחלה, שהיתה ראויה לילד בה' ולעמוד בו', ולהטיל בז' ולעמוד בח'. השתא מטילה יום ז' עם ו', כנגד ב' ימים שעמדה, כדי שתעמוד ביום ח', כפי שהיתה ראויה לחשבון הראשון:
Rashi on Niddah 39b:6:2.english: Or did it formulate [it] as from the outset - According to the calculation that it was supposed to lay from the outset: that it was supposed to lay on the fifth [day] and pause on the sixth, and lay on the seventh and pause on the eighth; now it lays on the seventh day together with the sixth, corresponding to the two days that it paused, in order that it will pause on the eighth day, as it was supposed to according to the original calculation.

Rashi on Niddah 39b:6:3.hebrew: על כרחך כדלקמיה נקטה - והא אשה נמי, כשחוזרת לוסתה לראות ליום כ"ב, לאו לפי חשבון הראשון, אלא ליום כ"ב לראייתה. הלכך, האי יומא הוא דאסרינן:
Rashi on Niddah 39b:6:3.english: Perforce [the Tanna] formulated [it] in accordance with what follows - And this woman as well, when she returns to her regular cycle to experience bleeding on the twenty-second day, [it is] not according to the initial reckoning, but rather on the twenty-second day from her [actual] bleeding. Therefore, it is this day that we forbid.

Rashi on Niddah 39b:7:1.hebrew: א"ל רב פפא אלא הא דאמר כו' אין אשה קובעת לה וסת תוך ימי נדותה - בימים שהיא נדה, כדבעינן לפרושי מילתא דרבי יוחנן: דחזאי ריש ירחא וה' בירחא, וריש ירחא וה' בירחא, והשתא חזאי בה' בירחא, דהוו להו ג' זימני בה' בירחא, ומעכשיו יהיה לה וסת בה' בחדש. לריש לקיש לא הוה וסת, דהא תרי זימני קמאי דה' בירחא הוי תוך ימי נדותה ממש, דהא נדה הויא מריש ירחא, ופעם ג' הוה ימי נדה לפי חשבון הראוי, שהיתה ראויה לראות ריש ירחא. ומדקרי לפעם ג' תוך ימי נדה, אלמא לפי חשבון הראוי מנינן:
Rashi on Niddah 39b:7:1.english: Rav Pappa said to him: But that which was said, etc., a woman does not establish a cycle for herself during the days of her menstruation - [Meaning,] on days when she is a menstruant, as we will explain Rabbi Yoḥanan's statement: Where she saw [blood] on the first of the month and on the fifth of the month, and on the first of the month and on the fifth of the month, and now she saw on the fifth of the month, so that there were three times on the fifth of the month, and from now on she will have an established cycle on the fifth of the month. According to Reish Lakish, it would not be an established cycle, for the first two times on the fifth of the month were literally within her days of menstruation, since she was a menstruant from the first of the month, and the third time was [considered] days of menstruation according to the expected calculation, as she had been expected to see on the first of the month. And since [the Gemara] calls the third time "within the days of menstruation," evidently we calculate according to the expected calculation.

Tosafot on Niddah 39b:9:1.hebrew: אלמא מריש ירחא מנינן - וא"ת: דילמא משום ראיה ראשונה קרי ליה תוך ימי נדה? ופרש"י, דדייק מדקאמר "קובעת תוך ימי נדותה", משמע דפעם ג' דהוא הקביעות הוי כימי נדתה, אלמא חשיב כאילו ראתה ריש ירחא. והקשה לו ריב"א: דלמה לא תירץ לו כגון שראתה ריש ירחא וה' בירחא שלשה זימני, דהשתא הוי ממש תוך ימי נדתה וקבעה וסת, ודיה שעתה אם תראה בחמשא בירחא של חדש ד', או שצריכה לפרוש מבעלה כל ה' בירחא עד שתעקור וסתה ג' פעמים? והשיבו רש"י: משום דבפ"ק (לעיל נדה דף יא.) מוקמינן דר' יוחנן במעיין סתום, משום דפריך אמתניתין דהתם, דקתני דבימי נדתה אינה צריכה בדיקה: ולבדוק דלמא קבעה לה וסת כרבי יוחנן! ולכך המקשה אוקי הכא מילתיה דר' יוחנן במעיין סתום, שראתה בג' ה' בירחא ולא בריש ירחא, דראייה שלישית היא ממעיין סתום. ומתניתין דפ"ק (שם דף יא.) כגון שראתה תרי זימני ריש ירחא וה' בירחא, ובשלישית, כי ראתה ריש ירחא, לא תבדוק בה' בירחא, שאפילו תראה לא קבעי' לה וסת, דמעיין פתוח הוא; אבל פעם ראשונה ושניה בודקת בימי נדה, שמא תראה בג' בה' בירחא ולא בריש ירחא. ולהכי לא הוה מצי לשנויי כגון דראתה ג' זימני ריש ירחא וה' בירחא, דא"כ הוה ליה מעיין פתוח; אלא משני כגון שראתה תרי זימני ריש ירחא לחוד, דהוי מעיין סתום, ובג' נמי, אע"ג דכבר ראתה בכ"ה, מה שראתה בריש ירחא חשיב מעיין סתום, כדמשני: דהא דחזאי בכ"ה דמים יתרים הוא דאתוספו בה. ועוד נראה לפרש, דהכא דייק דחשיב כאילו ראתה בג' בריש ירחא, דאי לאו הכי, אמאי קבעה לה וסת? הלא ראיה זו אינה מעין האחרות שבאו בימי נדותה! ומיהו תימה לומר: כיון כדמעיקרא נקטה, וחשיב כאילו ראתה ריש ירחא, כיון דאכתי לא קבעה לה וסת בריש ירחא, דלא דמי לההיא דלעיל דכבר קביע לה וסת לכ"ב, כדקאמר "היתה למודה לראות". ונראה לפרש, דמיירי כגון שראתה ג' זמני בריש ירחא וה' בירחא; ואין לחוש אם אין הש"ס מזכיר תלתא זימני, דה"נ בפ"ק (שם דף יא.) לא קאמר תלתא זימני גבי "קפצה וראתה". והא דנקט: "והשתא חזאי בה' בירחא ובריש ירחא לא חזאי", לאו משום דע"י ראייה זו השתא קבעה לה וסת, דהא קבעה לה כבר מג' זימני קמאי, אלא לומר לך שדיה שעתה בראייה זו, כדרבי דוסא, דאמר בפ"ק (לעיל נדה דף ד:) דאין דיה שעתה אלא בשעת וסת דוקא. ומיהו, אף בלא ראתה השתא הוה מצי למימר דקבעה לה וסת, לענין שאסורה בה' בירחא עד שתעקור הוסת ג' פעמים. והשתא מוכח, אע"ג דברביעי לא חזאי ריש ירחא, קבעה לה וסת בה' בירחא, משום דכיון שראתה ג' זימנין ה' בירחא, גם בחדש ד' חשוב כאילו ראתה ריש ירחא, וה"נ כ"ב מכ"ב מנינן. והוי מצי למימר: וליטעמיך, דאוקמית מילתיה דר' יוחנן במעין פתוח, א"כ תקשה מתני' דפ"ק (שם דף יא.) דקתני דאינה בודקת בימי נדה! א"נ, הא חשיב מעיין סתום, ומעיין פתוח יפרש כמו שפירש"י בלשון שני בפ"ק (שם יא.) שראתה אבג"ד, ובהכי איירי מתני דהתם, דבהכי לא קבעה לה וסתה:
Tosafot on Niddah 39b:9:1.english: Evidently, one counts from the first of the month - And if you should say: Perhaps because of the first sighting [in each cycle] it is called "within the days of her menstruation"? And Rashi explained that he deduced [this] from the fact that it says: "[A woman] fixes [a veset] within the days of her menstruation," which implies that the third time, which is the fixing [of the veset], is like the days of her menstruation; evidently, it is considered as though she saw [blood] on the first of the month. And Riva objected to him: Why didn't he answer him [by explaining the case as] where she saw [blood] on the first of the month and on the fifth of the month three times? For then [in that case], it is literally within the days of her menstruation, and she has established a fixed cycle (veset), and her time is sufficient (dayah sha'atah) if she sees [blood] on the fifth of the fourth month, or [the practical relevance is] that she is required to separate from her husband on every fifth of the month until she uproots her veset three times! And Rashi answered him: Because in the first chapter (above, Niddah 11a), we establish [the ruling] of Rabbi Yochanan as referring to an obstructed source (ma'ayan satum), because [the Gemara] raised an objection there against the Mishnah, which teaches that during the days of her menstruation she does not require an examination: "And let her examine [herself], lest she establish for herself a veset according to Rabbi Yochanan!" And therefore, the questioner [Rav Pappa] established Rabbi Yochanan's statement here as referring to an obstructed source, where on the third [month] she saw [blood] on the fifth of the month and not on the first of the month, so that the third sighting is from an obstructed source. And the Mishnah of the first chapter (ibid. 11a) is [referring to a case] such as where she saw [blood] twice on the first of the month and on the fifth of the month; and on the third [month], when she saw [blood] on the first of the month, she does not need to examine on the fifth of the month, because even if she were to see [blood], she would not establish a veset, for it is an open source (ma'ayan patuach). But the first and second time, she examines during the days of menstruation, lest on the third [month] she see on the fifth of the month and not on the first of the month [and thereby establish a veset from an obstructed source]. And therefore, he [Rav Huna son of Rav Yehoshua] could not answer [such] as where she saw three times on the first of the month and on the fifth of the month, because if so, it would be an open source! Rather, he answers [such] as where she saw twice on the first of the month alone, which is an obstructed source; and on the third [month] as well, even though she had already seen [blood] on the twenty-fifth, that which she saw on the first of the month is considered an obstructed source, as he answers: "that which she saw on the twenty-fifth was extra blood that gathered inside her." And furthermore, it seems [proper] to explain that here he deduced that it is considered as though she saw [blood] on the first of the month on the third [month], because if not so, why did she establish for herself a veset? Is this sighting not unlike the others, which occurred during the days of her menstruation?! However, it is astonishing to say: "since she resumed [bleeding], she resumed according to her original [pattern]" and it is considered as though she saw [blood] on the first of the month, given that she had not yet established a veset on the first of the month! For this is not comparable to that [case] above, where she had already established a veset for day twenty-two, as it says: "she was accustomed to seeing [blood on that day]." And it seems [proper] to explain that it deals with [a case] such as where she saw three times on the first of the month and on the fifth of the month; and there is no concern if the Shas does not mention three times, for similarly in the first chapter (ibid. 11a) it does not say three times regarding "she jumped and saw [blood]." And that which it stated: "and now she saw on the fifth of the month, and on the first of the month she did not see," is not because through this sighting she now establishes a veset, for she already established it from the first three times! Rather, [it is] to tell you that "her time is sufficient" (dayah sha'atah) regarding this sighting, in accordance with Rabbi Dosa, who said in the first chapter (above, Niddah 4b) that "her time is sufficient" applies only at the exact time of a veset. However, even without her seeing [blood] now, it could have said that she established a veset, with respect to the ruling that she is forbidden [to engage in marital relations] on the fifth of the month until she uproots the veset three times. And now it proves [Rav Pappa's deduction]: even though in the fourth [month] she did not see on the first of the month, she established a veset on the fifth of the month [meaning, the veset remains established for the fifth of the month within her menstruation], because since she saw three times on the fifth of the month, in the fourth month as well it is considered as though she had seen [blood] on the first of the month; and likewise [in our sugya], we count twenty-two from twenty-two! And [Rav Huna son of Rav Yehoshua] could have said: "And according to your reasoning, that you established Rabbi Yochanan's statement in [a case of] an open source, if so, the Mishnah of the first chapter (ibid. 11a) is difficult, which teaches that she does not examine during the days of menstruation!" Or alternatively: this [case] is considered an obstructed source; and "an open source" would be explained as Rashi explained in his second interpretation in the first chapter (ibid. 11a), where she saw [blood continuously on days] 1, 2, 3, 4; and it is with this that the Mishnah there deals, for in such a case she does not establish a veset.
